key_insight: PCA of full-field strain measurements reveals signatures of yielding and early strain localization that are less distinct in instantaneous strain maps.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help identify plasticity onset and failure-prone regions in aluminum components with different thermal exposure histories.
method: Measure sequential strain fields using Digital Image Correlation during uniaxial tensile loading.
Apply unsupervised Principal Component Analysis to extract temporal signatures and spatial deformation maps.
Compare the second-component projection peak with 0.2% offset yielding and inspect pre-transition localization.
evidence_signal: Tests on AA6063-T5 in as-received and 100°C, 200°C, and 300°C exposed conditions showed agreement between the second-component peak and offset yielding, while pre-transition component maps highlighted subsequent failure regions.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish generalization beyond this alloy and loading mode; early-localization analysis also relies on high-temporal-resolution strain measurements.
paper_title: Making Plasticity Visible: A Case Study for High-Temperature Exposed Aluminum Alloy
